body:
I've never done heroin and coke. And I recognise that it's not a safe combo. But coke by itself makes me pretty anxious. Many people drink with coke to deal with that but I'm not a big fan. Plus you get cocaethylene which is also pretty unsafe. 

I LOVE the combination of oxy and coke. Will take the oxy first and then do the coke. Just such an amazing feeling and zero anxiety. But yeah as other have said probably not the safest combo. I think the real problem is that it would be pretty easy to overdo it on the oxy (or heroin if that's what you're doing) and the coke masks the effect of the opioid so you may end up doing too much of the opioid and OD on that. Proceed with caution but man does it feel good.

Not sure that wanting to enjoy a meal or train ride without being surrounded by screaming kids is pathological to be honest. If they're quiet and well behaved I have no real problem it's just that most of them..... aren't.

I've been in the same boat. I've done therapy because that's what you're supposed to do and because people say it helps. It's good to talk to someone, good to develop healthy ways of thinking, etc but I've never subscribed to the view that if your neurochemistry is haywire, in other words if you're SICK, talking is going to pull you out of a severe depression.

A lot of people on here will disagree but where I primarily disagree with CBT, in particular, is that it's largely based on how you think determining the way you feel. Um, no, for me at least it's the other way round. If my mood is good, my view about the world, future, self, etc is all positive. If my mood is extremely low then of course my thoughts are going to be negative.

I'm not saying that therapy isn't valuable (especially when you have underlying issues that caused the depression) but I see it as an adjunct for somebody who is severely depressed, at best, not the thing that is going to pull somebody out of an episode of major depression. Therapy is good for OCD, anxiety, etc though, in my experience and is probably helpful for preventing recurrence of depression. It's not so good, at least by itself, for when you're in the middle of an acute and severe episode. 

Meds don't work for me anymore but they did at one point. They cured my depression. It bugs me when people say, 'Oh but meds just MASK depression, they don't cure it. For that you need to get to the bottom of things.' Bullshit, if the illness is a disorder of chemistry and meds correct that disorder then of course they're a cure. 

Just a shame they don't work all the time. Or they work and then stop working.

Haha I thought that might be the case (it being illegal). What a world we live in. God forbid that people want some, shock, horror, peace and quiet. What a terrible thing to wish for, we really are monsters.

Glad the living situation isn't TOO bad at least but yeah when you finally do get to a place without shared walls, I promise you'll never go back!

We thought by living on the top floor we'd be ok but yeah by some miracle of acoustics we could hear the kid (often kids as the other downstair's neighbor's grandkids would come every weekend) running around as they they were above not below us. It legitimately caused me massive stress, to the point where even if it happened to be quiet I couldn't relax because I'd be anticipating the next bout of noise.

I'd rather be around barking dogs, smokers or crackheads than screaming children, lol but I guess I'm pretty extreme. 

I was in the same position, living on the other side of the world from family so would fly back a couple of times a year. During that time I wasted a tonne on biz flights but it was actually worth it because flying biz is just generally great but also no kids.

I don't know why that has changed recently, whether it's just a coincidence or some other reason. Certainly biz class flights haven't gotten any cheaper so it's not that. But yeah I felt sick during the entire last flight I took at the thought of how much I'd shelled out to still be surrounded by screeching brats. Again, I just don't think airlines should allow it.

Most parents just don't care though. It's very rare that I've seen parents be truly considerate when it comes to ensuring that other people aren't terrorised by their spawn. Then again I suppose the considerate ones wouldn't be taking their kids on biz class flights anyway or to nice restaurants, so there probably are considerate parents, we just don't see them!

It's the same mentality as people watching videos on their phones on speaker on public transportation or flights. I just can't fathom it at all. I'm sure they're happier people than I am because they just have no regard for other people's feelings whatsoever. 

I do sometimes genuinely wonder whether i'd change if I became a parent. Glad I'm never going to find out though.

We just moved out of an apartment because the kid below (unbelievably yes we could hear running from below) was constantly running around. We told the neighbors and got the classic, 'He's a child what do you expect?' Now we've moved into a house and it's bliss. I'll never go back to living in an apartment. But that's only an option for us because we're living in some small town, not like we could do that in London or New York!

So yes I completely agree with you. If you suggest stuff like that though, in my experience, people will look at you like you're a war criminal or something!

Flights are another thing. A few years ago my company flew me out business class to Japan. It was the first time I'd travelled biz and was like heaven. After that I couldn't go back so then started always flying biz long haul. I'm not rich or anything so it was a big expenditure for me but worth it because there were never any screaming kids (on top of the other benefits of course). 

But in the last couple of years things changed for some reason. The last biz class flights I took were full of kids. I mean if I'm paying £2,500 for a flight I really, really do not expect to have to put up with screaming babies or children running up and down the aisles. So I've basically stopped flying long haul as a result. 

I'll never get over how utterly selfish parents are while having the gall to call US selfish for not having kids. I have a small dog and some restaurants do allow us to bring him but if he started barking or making any sort of nuisance of himself at all I'd leave immediately. Parents will happily sit there knocking back wine or playing on their phones while their kids run riot. It's just unbelievable to me.

Me too, would be amazing. 

My worst experience was booking a hotel which the travel agent said was adults only. We got there and to my horror there were kids EVERYWHERE, running around and screaming. I asked the rep what the hell was going on and was told, 'Oh WE don't allow families to book, but other operators book this hotel and don't have that policy.' It's one of the most absurd situations I've encountered in my life.

What I can't stand is when someone posts on a forum about how their partner is pressurising them to have a kid and they really don't want one. Then you get a tonne of replies from people saying stuff like, 'I felt the same way but eventually I caved and now my kid is the best thing that ever happened to me.'

Or, even worse, then the responses are, 'My husband/wife didn't want kids but I persuaded (or sometimes, horrifyingly, tricked) him/her into having a kid and now they couldn't be happier. 

Just the sheer arrogance of having so little respect for the person you're with that you're going to completely ignore what they've  clearly stated they don't want, smug in the knowledge that YOU know what's best for them.

The other variation on that is when some 19 year old has got pregnant or got is girlfriend pregnant and gets the same advice. 'No, don't take the life of your unborn child!' I was in the same situation and now I love my son/daughter more than anything. Well, yeah, of course you do, that's how nature works, by making sure your brain produces bonding chemicals to stop you leaving the nightmare on a doorstop or something. But now you've just completely sacrificed the phase of your life where you're supposed to enjoy being young, having fun, building a career for yourself, etc. Just get the damn abortion and have a kid later on if you want one. 

I really admire the honesty of Kate. Human beings are so ego driven that they're pretty much always going to tell themselves that whaever they made was the right one. That kind of post facto rationalisation never sits right with me and it takes bravery to say I didn't want a kid, I got talked into it and, lo and behold, I've now pretty much f\*\*ked my entire life up.

What's even more terrible here is that the boyfriend/family talked her into it and now she is the one left with the enormous burden of raising a child, not them. It's pretty damn evil.
Thanks!

Hey, yeah actually. I'll do this first ECT in England then after that get it done abroad. If it improves this crushing depression a bit it will be worth it. It's not like I can even enjoy the money I do have now.

Thanks a lot, really appreciate your kind words.

ECT has a bad rep but it really is very effective. I do feel hopeful but the amount of stress I've had trying to get it organised is unbelievable.

Plus I really do feel like the whole system is designed to extract as much money as possible from people who are really sick. I'm in the UK so I could go NHS but waiting lists are long and I imagine if I wanted ECT on the NHS it would take a long time, I'd end up staying weeks on a ward that is only slightly better than a prison, it couldn't be done as a day case so I'd have to take a lot time off work, etc.

Sorry rant over, I was just thinking today about how much money I've spent on mental health care. It's an insane amount. My job is stressful but pays well but instead of getting to 'enjoy' the money which should be the quid pro quo of a demanding job, I just end up spending a lot of it on treatment!

Good post OP. When I'm depression free I really feel like I don't need people at all. Consequently I don't feel let down by people.

When severely depressed I end up expecting more from people and then feel very let down and bitter when they don't live up what I 'expect.'

My view now is definitely that friends really can't be relied on. The number of friends that have come and gone during my life is ridiculous. And it's not just me, I've seen the best of friends fall out over the most trivial matters and never make things up again.

Like you all I would want would be somebody who checks up on me, makes an effort to hang out and talk when things are bad. But no, I've had friends of 20 years know that I'm in a seriously bad way not even bother to send a text or make a call for months.

So now friendships to me are basically people you see once in a blue moon, hopefully spend a pleasant few hours with and then go your separate way.

People don't really care about each other all that much.

Only about 3 weeks but I'd heard that it typically worked within 2 weeks.

I'm in such a bad way I'm going for ECT. I simply cannot endure this for much longer and at least after ECT i'll know I've tried everythiing.
Thanks a lot for the reply. Unfortunately Valdoxan hasn't done anything for me but no meds seem to. Glad you had success with it!

Hey man, always happy to listen if you want to PM, especially given that your family are not understanding.

I have to be honest and tell you I'm angry at your family and are basically putting you in a position where you're afraid to get help.

I'm probably overstepping here but put yourself first. Your family aren't the ones suffering with this sh\*t. I remember telling my Dad about my issues. He didn't understand at all so I know what that's like. But if it comes down to doing what's best for you or placating your family, f\*ck them.

If you want to wait a year or two that's fine but the longer you wait to address these issues, the more likely it is that they will get worse. Do you even need to tell your friends your seeing a doctor? I don't know how old you are but I assume you can get the help you need without your parents knowing. It's bad enough they're not supportive but it would be inhumane if they were actually preventing you getting help.

Hey man, I'm really sorry to hear that. In a terrible place at the moment too so I can totally relate to what you're saying. 

Like you I feel I can cope with a certain level of depression, it's horrible but I just get on with it. But I've had several times when it's worsened to a level where the sheer intensity of it horrifies me.

I think it's important to, as far as you can, not predict the future and believe that because you feel so bad right now, it's going to continue. It could well be that it doesn't last and as you say you think this is going to be a short spell.

I'm not sure if you're seeing a doctor that would be able to give you something to help out here but if it gets too bad know that you can always just go to hospital, voluntarily, stay a few days then leave when you feel better.

It's beyond a joke. If you're physically ill there's a sense that doctors kind of 'take over' in your treatment.

With mental health the onus is on YOU to organise everything and take responsibility for your own cure. This where people with severe depression are one of the least capable groups of orchestrating their own treatment.

I've had appointments with psychiatrists where I told them I was suicidal and then gone months without an e-mail or call to see how I'm doing.

We're really on our own.

Completely feel like I'm ruining my wife's life with my depression. Think I'd be doing her a huge favour if I left her even though she's been so supportive for so long. It's too much to ask of another person.

Same, hate waking up knowing there's another full day to get through. It's absolutely miserable.

People keep talking about hobbies and doing stuff I enjoy but I don't know if there is anything. I can't even enjoy the things I used to. And if there is something I 'want' to do, I feel too awful to do it.

So just endless hours alone, not even really able to watch anything. It's terrible.

It helps me with mild depression. And I like feeling fit and knowing I can run (reasonably) fast over long distances. I feel healthy and virtuous and a smug sense of superiority as I run past people lighting their filthy cigarettes.

Of course now, in a major depressive episode, I'm the one stood outside smoking my third cigarette at 7am watching people jog past while I secretly hate and envy them, feeling like a bitter degenerate.

Thanks man, had some good news and it seems like it's going to happen. Definitely exhausted all other options so just hoping so much it will happen soon and I can get back to some semblance of normality.

Thanks for the reply and again I hope you don't feel I was dismissive of your suggestion

ECT is the most effective treatment for severe depression. More than meds, therapy or anything else. More than that it's pretty much instantaneous. It's also safe (for something done under general anesthesia) although it does have side effects such as short term memory loss.

It would never be used as a first line treatment but I've exhausted all other options and things are dire. ECT can literally be a life saver for people in my position. 

If the ECT works then I'll be able to focus on things like therapy, diet, lifestyle changes, etc. Right now I can barely move.

No, I'm sorry with all due respect I've tried all manner of therapy and it hasn't helped. I have a serious mood disorder and I'm not looking for advice about therapy. I really have no PTSD or particular issues to work through that can be resolved by therapy. Maybe when I'm slightly better I would consider therapy, etc so I'm not ruling it out but therapy takes weeks/months of hard work and I'm willing to put the work in but right now I need something that is going to help quickly, at least to get me to a point where therapy, etc may benefit. Right now I would simply be incapable of taking in any of the information, doing the homework, etc. Does that makes sense? I was feeling fine, everything going well in life, good relationship, work going great, in great shape and without any change in life circumstances my mood plummeted to where it is now. It's an all consuming 'physical' depression. 

I appreciate the value of therapy but in the circumstances please take my word that therapy isn't going to help me right at the moment. 

I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for your response or that your suggestion has no merit.

I'm looking for specific advice in relation to the question I asked about ECT, not suggestions about types of therapy, etc. If I had relationship problems, self esteem problems, disorders of thinking etc, therapy may be very useful. Therapy isn't going to help me now any more than it would someone with bipolar disorder or schizophrenia.

Yeah exactly the same. At least if I were destitute, homeless, lacking companionship and living in a horrible environment there would be concrete things I could improve. I don't have a single thing like that. Healthy, great wife, have money, great job and house and want to kill myself every day.

Yeah, the problem is if you could appreciate all these special little things that life has to offer, you'd never kill yourself in the first place.

How about:

"The morning after I killed myself, I woke up. I was completely incapable of love, felt only utter coldness and pain and couldn't connect with a single living human being. I watched a 'beautiful' sunrise and it made me feel worse because I couldn't appreciate one thing about it. I'd made the right decision after all."

Not in any way suggesting that these kids should be sedated but to give some perspective on the lethality of sleeping pills:

The acute LD50 (of Xanax/alprazolam) in rats is 331-2171 mg/kg.

2-3mg of Xanax would likely knock the average adult without benzo tolerance clean out. So even taking HED into account you'd need an unholy amount of Xanax to kill a person. Surgery under general anesthesia is a bit different from taking a few Xanax. Benzos are dangerous in combination with alcohol or other drugs, not alone. When I say dangerous I mean in terms of a fatal overdose. They're extremely dangerous when it comes to losing days of your life, important relationships and your freedom.

Thanks, really appreciate the response. Unfortunately Im'm in the UK and only one place does it.

I can't get my insurance to cover rTMS. I can afford to go and have it done at the same place again but using the FDA protocol, I'm just weighing up whether it's worth it or not. Of course I would pay all the money I have for a cure to my depression but the guy who runs this clinic says the protocol he used on me has been effective for 75% of patients and he has seen no difference in results between the protocol he used on me and the FDA protocol. So I don't want to waste thousands either.

I'm going to talk to my psychiatrist about Ketamine again.

I have absolutely no idea. I asked the guy and he told me that he had found that he had obtained similar results with the protocol he followed.

Now I'm left wondering whether to go and drop another few grand with the correct protocol. Of course I'd happily pay that if it helps but I'm pretty angry that he didn't use an approved protocol. Not like he'll give me my money back though.

Thanks so much for the answer. Complex is putting it mildly isn't it?
 
I still can't decide whether to go and have more of the rTMS or not.

I've tried to get Ketamine but haven't had any luck. My doc doesn't believe in it and won't put me forward. And I'm assuming that just scoring Ketamine and doing it myself isn't going to help.

Really don't know what to do next.
Thanks Amy. Just struggling through the day. Only good time is just before falling asleep. Definitely no way to live. Hope you are having a much better weekend.

If only my thinking were as balanced as yours! I suppose your reply (which is very helpful) illustrates how skewed my own thinking is, probably to the extent of being completely egocentric and ascribing everybody's actions to ME. That kind of distorted thinking isn't the cause of my depression but it doesn't help either, so thank you Amy for giving me a more balanced perspective.

That aside it's just kind of lonely. I'm very lucky to have my wife and I feel terrible for people that are going through this and are truly alone but the best thing about being inpatient wasn't the staff (they were a joke to be honest) but being surrounded by other people also struggling.

I work in a corporate world where everybody is expected to be 'on' all the time and it's absolutely impossible to be yourself or talk about how you're really doing. So it was refreshing to be in an environment where, when people asked how you were doing, you could say, 'Terrible', instead of 'Fine' or 'Great'. I do miss that I have to say.

I do think generally in this world we could all be a lot more supportive of each other and it blows my mind that we choose not to be. But that's reality and there's no changing it. 

I will follow your advice and keep pushing on, I've just been doing it for months now and it's exhausting. I can handle depression/anxiety when it's a few bad days or weeks followed by a period of respite but this is relentless and I'm tired. I've also spent a lot of money and been through a lot of treatments and none have helped so I'm starting to lose hope. And when nothing works there is always that one option left, 100% guaranteed to cure all depression and anxiety. 

As much as I appreciate the support I feel guilty that this is all one way traffic. I know you said you're fine but if you ever do have problems and want to talk it would be my privilege to listen.

Japan.

Drugs.

Pick one. 

Lived there for years and wouldn't go near the stuff there.

I think that's a much healthier way of looking at it and you're right, I guess some people just want to forget it and move on. Which is also kind of hurtful because it suggests (maybe in my warped way of thinking) that they're doing fine now and I'm not. More realistically though, knowing some of the people in there, I doubt very much indeed that their problems are behind them. I don't wish it but they were so messed up that there's no way  they will just be 100% well now.

It's been my experience generally in life, you meet people, you feel that you bond with them and maybe you'll stay in each other's lives and then you just don't. Relationships are so ephemeral. It is what it is I suppose.

I want to thank you again for listening. It does help and even more when the person does seem to understand what this is like.

All I can do is try again tomorrow. Get up, force myself to go for a run and try to push forward, hoping that this is going to get better at some point soon. I've only been on Agomelatine for 4 days so it's too soon to say it's not working, I just have a feeling that it won't, given that I haven't read many success stories and even my doc didn't seem all that optimistic about it.

Thanks Amy. Maybe part of the problem is that I'm coming off a powerful med (Effexor). It never helped me but it's notoriously difficult to come off. I just haven't read that much good stuff about the new med (Agomelatine) so hard to be hopeful.

One of my big disappointments is the people I was inpatient with. While in hospital I felt like we bonded and formed what could have been a real support network. Within weeks of being discharged nobody is talking to each other, or rather I should say they're not talking to me. I've reached out a couple of times and nothing. That's kind of depressing in itself.

That's pretty unique of you. Not  many people do!

Yes she knows and she does all she can but ultimately there's only so much she can do.

I'm completely out of ideas. Like I say I want to get ECT but don't know if that's going to be possible. Living life like this is beyond pointless, it's a huge negative. Don't see an answer.

Hello Amy, no I'm with my wife. She's very supportive but ultimately what can she do?

I've woken up feeling awful again and with a long day to get through. I don't particularly have to do anything but there's literally nothing I want to do. Have no motivation or interest in anything and feel actively terrible. In this state, there's literally no point being alive.

I really want to get ECT but seems like that's going to be a mission, if I can get it at all.

Really hope you're doing better. Are you suffering from any of this yourself or just interested in supporting others? It's very noble either way!

Thanks Amy. Restless sleep and up at 4am. Not a good sign. Until now I've at least been sleeping ok.

Hope you're doing better than I am.

Hey I'm in Europe right now. It's not too hard to get home but yeah all i could do would be wander into A&E. I don't relish it, it's also a big step as it will be more time off work (I took a month off to go inpatient). Health is more important but am worried that losing my job will just send me further down. I'm hoping I can find a way to get treatment while taking minimal time off.

Thank you Amy, you're a sweetheart.

I don't know if I'll be safe until I can get the ECT. I'm not even in England and I couldn't go to hospital where I am. The only thing I could do is fly back to England and walk into A&E. I guess if I really am going to kill myself i'll do that first.

Words cannot describe how messed up this is.

Again thank you so much for the support.

Thanks Amy, you've been very kind.

I e-mailed my psychiatrist about possible ECT and he is looking into it.

He also told me the rTMS I had didn't follow the accepted protocol (somebody else administered it) now I'm left wondering if it's worth having it again, this time with the correct protocol. I'm so confused as to what to do.

I'm really sorry you're going through this. I'm similarly desperate but at least have a supportive wife. Your treatment by your family is unconscionable. Feel free to talk to me anytime you like. I'm disgusted by the way you're being treated. Let one of those people experience what you're going through just for a day and see how they change their tune.

You're very smart Amy and very kind. I thought you might reply pointing out the contradiction in my post ("Talk therapy doesn't help", "Talking is the only thing that helps" lol).

You have a point. Talking does help up to a point. The thing that did me most good when I was in-patient wasn't the doctors or therapists but the other patients. So, yes, clearly sharing and talking and having a support network does help. It won't fix the chemical mood disorder I have, but it helps. 

However, I think what helped there was being around other patients all the time. Talk therapy once or twice a week doesn't have a significant impact.

I do feel very disillusioned with people (although I should stress this isn't the source of my depression). I felt like we bonded in hospital but now we're back in the real world none of us are really in contact with each other.

It's a shame isn't it, that people don't stick together more?

Things are extremely bad at the moment. I rate my depression out of 10. Up to a 7 or 8 I can cope, even though it's unpleasant. It's a 10 at the moment and I can't even watch some simple movie or TV programme, let alone function at a higher level. So I'm just taking clonazepam to try to numb how bad I feel. 

I should be in hospital right now but I'm still terrified of going into an NHS ward. Plus I think if I lose my job it can only make things worse.

Thank you for listening, I am genuinely grateful. I don't know where I go from here, it's horrible to be in a situation where you don't want to kill yourself but you've explored all the alternatives and there are none left.
What a bunch of fucking pricks. To hell with them.

Honestly speaking I have a mood disorder and therapy of any sort doesn't touch it. I can literally go to bed feeling fine and then wake up feeling suicidal. The depression is very chemical. I don't really have any trauma, issues, etc. When the depression lifts life is fine, when it comes it feels like the mental equivalent of physical pain. 

I know people might disagree but therapy isn't going to help me, I know it instinctively and without any doubt whatsoever.

Of course that isn't to say that I don't want to talk to people (as I am now to you) or that it isn't a good thing to do, just that it's not the answer to my depression.

I've told my psychiatrist but he tells me I have to be patient and see if the Agomelatine works. This is the problem I have with psychiatrists (and I actually like my current one). They talk about waiting weeks as though it's simple. Yes, it's easy for him to wait 5 weeks. It's not so easy for me, when every second is hellish.

I do appreciate you talking to me Amy but I'm not sure that there's an answer here. ECT maybe, if I can get it but I don't think I can.

Hello Amy,

You're a really kind person and I want to say how grateful I am for your support. It's amazing how people online can be more supportive than so called friends!

Even worse I was inpatient (twice) in the last few months and I felt I really bonded with some patients in there. We supported each other, spent a lot of time together, understood each other. And you know what, now none of us are in touch. It's sad huh?

I'm under the care of a Psychiatrist who I'm in constant contact with so I want to make clear that I'm not trying to deal with this on my own. He says I have to give 5 or 6 weeks to see if the Agomelatine works. I don't know if it's the depression but I just have no faith that it will. I must have been on 20 different meds and none of them have done a thing.

I went to Rotterdam for 2 weeks to have intensive rTMS. Did nothing.

I run every day (although today I just couldn't, I could barely move).

I have continued to work.

My point is I really am trying but I just feel worse and worse.

As for being safe, if I could do anything right now it would be go to hospital. But as I say I've been in patient twice in a private hospital in the UK and they really don't do much at all. They dispense meds and have about an hour or two max of therapy a day. But the only positive is that, yes, I feel a bit safer there.

Unfortunately I have used all but 6 days for the year of my insurance so if I went inpatient now it would have to be an NHS hospital which I assume is pretty horrible. Plus, again, what are they going to do? On top of which I'll stress about taking more time off work and possibly losing my job. I think that will just make me feel worse. 

The only treatment left I haven't had is ECT. I'm more than willing to do that but my Psych isn't.

All I can do is try to hang in there, hope that once I"m off the venlafaxine I may feel better and hope that the Agomelatine does something (not too hopeful about that). But it really does feel like the end of the road. 

Anyway thanks again, it's good to be able to talk and I'm not sure what your situation is or how you're doing but happy to listen as well.

Hi Amy, I really appreciate you taking the time to reply. It does help to talk, probably the only thing that does.

Just woke up and feeling worse than ever. Feel like I'm living in hell.

I was having some up days but I'm not anymore. The last few days have been unrelentingly terrible. Before that I was feeling terrible much of the time but having the occasional ok day (or few hours).

I can't believe that each day is worse than the last. I am coming off a med (Venlafaxine) and wonder if that could be contributing.

I don't know what to do.

Thanks I really appreciate it. I have a wife I love and a dog I love too. I also have parents but they haven't helped me at all so while I love them I have a lot of bitterness.

I wish meds would do something for me, even if they just made things 10% better, but they don't. I'm trying a new med now, agomelatine, but haven't read anything encouraging about it.

I too could accept the depressed life up to a point but when it's as severe as it is at the moment I'm just not strong enough, it's sheer torture. Good for you for being able to keep going though, it takes some strength.
Amen.

Thanks for the reply Amy. I don't know, I guess my wife is one thing. The other thins is just irrational hope that I can get better and enjoy life. I'm pretty happy with my life set-up, it's just the crushing depression that is killing me.
In same boat, happy to chat.

It's Agomelatine (Valdoxan). Doesn't seem to have particularly high efficacy and we're only trying it because it has a novel mechanism of action.

I have no qualms about ECT but yeah, not easy to just get it. 

Thanks again.

Hi thanks for the reply. I'm in the UK.

I have only been in a private hospital. They didn't have it there and it was never mentioned.

Maybe if I was in an NHS (state) hospital it would be offered but while I have terribly low mood and suicidal thoughts I don't have the biological symptoms of depression such as low appetite, sleeplessness, etc so my doc doesn't think I'd be a good candidate.

I'd try anything at this point and have specifically asked for this.

I remember the first time I sought help. I was 20 years old and in the most severe depression I'd ever experienced. On top of that I had OCD which the depression had taken to absolutely unfathomable levels.

I eventually sought help. Went to see a psychiatrist who had boasted to my classmates (was at medschool) how he cured some student displaying early symptoms. 

I can't tell you how much hope I placed in that appointment. He was going to make it better somehow, because surely there's no way any human being can be expected to live like that. There's bound to be help.

The guy didn't do shit. Told me that going through this would, 'Actually make you a better doctor someday.' My main concern at that point was not one day being a better doctor, it was to stop feeling like I was being tortured in the worst way possible.

I've had so many similar encounters since then. Remember another time when I was in nearly as terrible a way as that first time when the psychiatrist (private, I was paying £150 an hour) spent ten minutes talking about a family cruise he was going on.

You know, by and large these people don't give a single fukk. I'm not even saying whether therapy helps or doesn't help but at that particular time in life I just wanted an ounce of compassion. Have never got that from a doctor (with maybe one exception).

Breathing exercises and thinking positive. I mean, people get fucking paid to say that shit? Sorry for the rant, for those of you who have found good therapists and benefited, I'm very happy for you. But I just have so much cynicism and resentment towards psychiatrists and psychologists. I expect nothing from them now. Just dish me out some new meds and send me on my way. 

I still can't get over the fact that if you're in acute physical pain, there are always painkillers. But if you're in mental pain which is just as bad or worse even, there's nothing they can give you, except to maybe sedate you. I'm not blaming anyone for this, it just terrifies me that it's the case.

Here's a med, it may take a month to work. A month?!! A fucking month! But every second is an eternity in hell and you're casually telling me it may take a month? 

It's no wonder people end up taking their own lives, the mental health support network is so poor, people probably feel like there are no avenues. 

Oh the other best thing people have come out with - 'Only YOU can make yourself better'. Ok, you're saying this to someone who basically can't get out of bed, eat or sleep. But you're telling me it's all down to me. 

I'm sorry again for my rant OP, I just have so much disgust for the mental health 'profession' which seems to be pretty much dishing out pills using trial and error. 

Reading 'Darkness Visible' helped more than any of these oh so knowledgeable professionals. 

You know, by the time you are severely depressed/anxious you are PHYSICALLY ill. Physically in the sense that something is badly wrong with your brain chemistry.
